GUMPY - TEST REPORT  (build of 19 Oct 2026)
==========================================

RESULT: everything below passed on the final build.

1. RULES ENGINE - node test/engine.test.js  ->  20,568 checks passed, 0 failed
   - All 75 character IDs: numbering, categories, names, quips, sounds, voice lines,
     sprite files on disk, sprites embedded in the handheld page.
   - Card generation: 20,000 cards all valid (right column per letter, FREE center,
     no duplicate characters), no two identical cards; six different cards per round;
     fresh cards every round; call deck = all 75, no repeats.
   - Same seed -> identical cards and call order (replay); same seed + same inputs ->
     identical whole match.
   - All five patterns: one square short = FALSE GUMPY, complete = verified GUMPY;
     a plain row does not win Big X.
   - Marking: uncalled characters rejected, double marks rejected, late marks allowed.
   - Claims: false-claim penalty + lock, duplicate claim not processed twice,
     simultaneous claims inside the 1.5 s window both count, claims after the round
     closes are rejected, verified winners can't be undone.
   - Elimination: lowest completion -> fewest legit marks -> digital coin; 6,5,4,3,2
     active players across rounds; round winner never eliminated; everyone-co-wins case;
     call limit ending; all-75-called last-chance window; final always has a champion.
   - Every active power (cost, cooldown, once-per-round, no-instant-win rule, shield,
     reverse, hit immunity refund) and every chaos event (keeps legit marks + valid cards).
   - Every ghost power (haunt is temporary, possess keeps characters and marks,
     poltergeist delay lands, phantom shield blocks, storm once per round, ghost energy
     and action limits). Ghosts can't mark, claim or target ghosts.
   - Pause/resume shifts every timer; handheld views carry no other player's card and no deck.
   - 600 random full matches (aggressive bots: powers, ghosts, false claims) checked
     continuously: cards always valid, legit marks never removed, calls never repeat,
     exactly one elimination after rounds 1-4, champion every time.
     Match length with bots: avg 23.0 min (median 23.0, max 25.5).
     Avg calls per round: R1 28, R2 57, R3 67, R4 60, R5 71.

2. SIX-HANDHELD END-TO-END - python test/e2e.py  ->  16 passed, 0 failed
   Real gumpy_8784_addon.py loading a stand-in 8784 server file, big screen loaded
   from the add-on, six separate 720x720 handheld browsers that act ONLY through their
   buttons (A, B, X, Y, D-pad), game clock at 6x speed:
   - Server's own routes still work through the add-on.
   - All six handhelds connect; a second device asking for an occupied seat is refused.
   - Round intro on every handheld; no handheld ever receives another player's card.
   - Handheld 3 unplugged mid-round: big screen shows it offline after ~12 s; reopened,
     it got the same seat and the same card back.
   - Full 5-round match to a champion: 346 marks (0 rejected), 45 powers through the
     handheld power menu + target picker, 40 ghost attacks landed from ghost handhelds,
     13 GUMPY claims from the Y button, one ghost after each of rounds 1-4.
   - No script errors on the big screen or any handheld.

3. SCREENS CHECKED BY EYE (screenshots)
   Big screen: splash, title, lobby, round intro, live calling, GUMPY verification,
   celebration, results + ghost ceremony, final round with 4 ghost panels, champion.
   Handheld: lobby, intro, live card, call banner, powers menu, target picker,
   ghost screen, results, champion. Sandbox mode (6 handhelds on one screen) played
   by mouse on seat 1.


NOT DONE / NOT VERIFIED - please read
-------------------------------------
1. Your real files were not attached: no Arcadium OS files, no working game example,
   no Multi-Vibe 8784 server file. I used the exact add-on pattern from your
   3 Monkey Mayhem / Dirty Deeds builds (it loads your server and uses its Handler,
   PORT and ip()). Tested against a stand-in with those names, NOT your real server.
2. Not tested on real RG Rotates or the real Arcadium PC. A, B and the D-pad use the
   same mapping as your other games. X (find), Y / START (GUMPY!) and L / R (pick power)
   are new and unconfirmed on the hardware. Touch works for everything as a fallback.
3. Exit back to Arcadium OS: no launcher code was supplied, so EXIT sends an
   "arcadium:exit" message to the parent window, then closes / goes back.
   This needs checking against how Arcadium OS actually closes games.
4. Arcadium splash: the square red/black/silver splash art was not attached here, so
   the loading screens show a code-drawn ARCADIUM "A" placeholder. Send the image and
   it drops straight in.
5. Character names: G1-G15 are from your G-column sheet; UFO Abduction (U16), Mutant
   Banana (M31), Pirate Pug (P46) and Yeti Mayhem (Y61) are from the overview sheet.
   The other 56 names are PLACEHOLDERS I made up (flagged "provisional" in
   GUMPY_characters.json).
6. Your sheets disagree on G numbers. The production grid puts Gear Shark at G8, but the
   G-column sheet and every call example say G7 Gear Shark, so I followed the G-column
   sheet. The grid's G9 (sunglasses gorilla), G14 (gold monkey) and G15 (robot) are not
   used. Galactic Alien, Golden Banana and Goat Wizard had no grid icon, so their card
   icons are square cuts from the G-column art (slightly different style).
   Some characters look alike across columns (alien G2/U16, banana G3/M31/Y62,
   yetis U19/Y61/Y65/Y74, yin-yang P58/Y67) - that's in the source art.
7. Sprites are cut from flat poster images, so they are JPEGs with their dark tile
   backgrounds, not transparent PNGs (you asked for JPEG for Android anyway).
   Every sprite is a separate file in assets\.
8. Host poses: idle, talking, title, hype, laughing, results and party come from your
   art. Angry, shocked and ghost-invasion are the same art with red / flash / ghost
   effects - there is no dedicated art for them.
9. Animation: every call uses one shared animated reveal (zoom, rays, flash, wobble).
   G1-G15 and Mutant Banana use the big scene art; the others use the enlarged icon.
   No per-character animation frames exist in the art.
10. Sounds are built-in synth placeholders on named hooks (every character gets its own
    3-note jingle). Host voice uses the PC's built-in speech voice and is optional.
11. Pacing: ~23 minutes per match with 5.5 s per call and turbo (3.5 s) after 30 calls.
    Rounds 2-5 need 55-73 calls. Change the marking window in F9 if it feels slow/fast.
12. Collectibles / DCU ownership and trading: not in this version (as the brief said).
